newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened slightly against the dollar on Wednesday but rose against the basket of key foreign currencies following the rise of the dollar against the mark, dealers said.
"The basket is already touching the lower edge of the currency band, but the Bank of Israel still remains outside the market," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"If this trend continues the central bank will have to intervene on Thursday," she added.
They noted that the basket traded most of the day nearly seven percent below the diagonal rate.

The shekel fluctuates in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
Dealers attributed the shekel's recent strength to an upsurge in foreign currency-linked borrowing by the Israeli business sector.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2470 shekels against 3.2440 shekels on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6145 shekels against 3.6193 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8040 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8099 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0636 shekels against 2.0766 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2460 shekels.
